paper.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning
paper.abstract: Multimodal large language models can write code and interpret rendered images of 3D designs, but it remains unclear whether they can produce executable parametric 3D programs that are geometrically precise, semantically aligned and assembly-consistent. We introduce P3D-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates this ability under a unified protocol across three task families: text-conditioned part synthesis, image-conditioned multi-part reconstruction and image-plus-annotation assembly composition, with metrics that jointly probe executability, geometric fidelity, topology, text-grounded constraints, multiview semantic alignment and part-level assembly structure.

Add one remove-material feature made only from 2 separate circular profiles, not a connected slot or rectangular pocket. The main piece is a single solid extrusion with a long flat top and a rounded arched lower outline, not a stack of separate blocks. The visible underside void should remain curved, with straight vertical solid portions at the ends and a continuous slab across the top. In addition to the arched body outline, there is a paired circular material-removal pattern placed on the upper side; those circular features are cuts or recesses, not raised bosses. The circular removals use a shallower depth than the main body, so the model has a stepped-depth relationship while the surrounding material stays solid.

Use a main base reference span of length 0.75, width 0.421875, and height 0.191921, with the lower base extrusion extending 0.1919 upward from the base datum. Form this lower base from separate rounded profiles within the full 0.75 by 0.4218 span rather than as a filled rectangular plate: place one circular profile with its axis 0.2109 from the left edge and 0.2109 from the front edge, radius 0.2109, and place a second concentric circular group with its axis 0.6094 from the left edge and 0.2109 from the front edge, using radius 0.1406 with an inner radius of 0.1055 for the opening. Preserve the additional curved and slot-like profile portions in the lower sketch as rounded cut or boundary shapes, so the openings remain true voids rather than surface markings. Add the taller circular solid section over the left-side circular axis within a 0.4218 by 0.4218 footprint, offset 0 from the left edge, 0.3282 from the right edge, and 0 from both front and back edges; this upper-side material reaches 0.4424 from the same base datum, making it a taller continuation above the shallow base rather than an added segment stacked on top of the base height. Keep the upper circular section hollow/annular where the inner loop is present, including the rounded slot-like interruptions in the opening. Add a separate solid rectangular upright tab with length 0.041188, width 0.070313, and height 0.441346; position it with left offset 0.0703, right offset 0.6385, front offset 0.1758, and back offset 0.1757, and extrude it upward 0.4413 from the base datum.

The model is built from rounded circular sections with real central openings, so the visible collars should read as hollow/annular rather than solid disks. A lower rounded base links the larger and smaller circular areas, with curved outlines rather than a simple rectangular plate between them. The taller round section rises from one side of the lower form and has an inner opening with slot-like rounded interruptions at the top. A narrow solid rectangular upright tab is added beside the tall round body and reaches nearly the same height, while the lower base remains much shallower.

Abstract:
A thick rectangular slab with stepped solid protrusions underneath.

Detailed CAD facts:
The model is a rectangular slab with only added rectangular solids attached to its underside. Four shallow underside pads sit near the perimeter, and each pad carries a narrower, deeper rectangular continuation below it, producing a two-tier underside protrusion pattern. The deeper continuation in each pair is contained within the shallow pad footprint and shares either the left or right vertical edge along with the front and back edges. Treat all of these underside features as solid added material; there are no holes, cut-throughs, recesses, or engraved top-face details.

Abstract:
A rectangular frame plate with raised round collars around corner holes.

Detailed CAD facts:
The part is a thin rectangular base with a large rectangular opening cut through the middle, leaving a continuous border frame. Four raised circular collars sit on the upper face near the corners of the frame rather than on any rectangular pads. Each collar is annular, with a central round hole that continues through the base. The rectangular center cut is a removed through area, and the circular centers are also removed material, while only the surrounding ring portions are added material. The model has stepped depth behavior: the base is shallow, the collars rise above it, and the central and circular cuts extend through the relevant thickness rather than forming raised features.
